bib.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale

SOURCE: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale, Dosovitskiy, Beyer, Kolesnikov, Weissenborn, Zhai, Unterthiner, Dehghani, Minderer, Heigold, Gelly, Uszkoreit, Houlsby. ICLR 2021 (arXiv:2010.11929v2, 3 Jun 2021).

COVERAGE: I read all 1,378 lines of the supplied extraction, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ramsey-wise-workspace-learn-ai-engineering/258b4f47-0655-4d5a-91fc-4d7f1120336b/scratchpad/txt/2010.11929.txt, 68,004 bytes by `wc -c`. I did not measure a character count and did not re-extract from the PDF. That covers pp. 1-22, including all appendices and Tables 1-9; references were read for origins. I read all 663 lines of the note. Figure captions came from `figures.py captions`, which truncates long ones. I did not view the figures as images, so plotted values are unread.

CLAIMS
- claim: Pre-trained at scale, ViT matches or beats the best CNNs on image benchmarks.
  number: 88.55% ImageNet, 77.63% VTAB
  setup: ViT-H/14, JFT-300M pre-training, fine-tuned at 518 with Polyak averaging, mean of 3 fine-tuning runs
  quote: "the best model reaches the accuracy of 88.55% on ImageNet, 90.72% on ImageNet-ReaL, 94.55% on CIFAR-100, and 77.63% on the VTAB suite of 19 tasks."
  where: p2; Table 2 p6
- claim: ViT took far less pre-training compute than the CNN baselines, though the authors say schedule and optimizer may also affect this.
  number: 2.5k and 0.68k against 9.9k and 12.3k core-days
  setup: columns are ViT-H/14 JFT, ViT-L/16 JFT, ViT-L/16 I21k, BiT-L, Noisy Student, on TPUv3
  quote: "TPUv3-core-days 2.5k 0.68k 0.23k 9.9k 12.3k"
  where: Table 2 p6
- claim: ViT overfits more than a ResNet of comparable cost on small datasets and overtakes it on large ones.
  number: 9M against 90M+
  setup: random JFT subsets, no extra regularisation, early stopping, few-shot linear accuracy; results plotted only (Fig 4)
  quote: "ViT-B/32 is slightly faster than ResNet50; it performs much worse on the 9M subset, but better on 90M+ subsets."
  where: p7
- claim: Larger pre-training sets raise ViT's ImageNet accuracy, most of all for larger variants.
  number: B/16 77.91, 83.97, 84.15; L/16 76.53, 85.15, 87.12
  setup: top-1, fine-tuned at 384, no Polyak averaging; regularisation tuned per dataset (Table 3)
  quote: "ImageNet 77.91 73.38 76.53 71.16 -" / "ImageNet 83.97 81.28 85.15 80.99 85.13" / "ImageNet 84.15 80.73 87.12 84.37 88.04"
  where: Table 5 p15
- claim: Without strong regularisation on mid-sized data, ViT falls below comparable ResNets.
  number: none
  setup: ImageNet-sized training, "ResNets of comparable size"
  quote: "yield modest accuracies of a few percentage points below ResNets of comparable size"
  where: p1
- claim: ViT reaches the same transfer performance as ResNets with less compute.
  number: 2-4x
  setup: JFT-300M pre-training, average over 5 datasets, controlled scaling study
  quote: "ViT uses approximately 2− 4× less compute to attain the same performance (average over 5 datasets)."
  where: p8
- claim: Having a position embedding matters; its form barely does.
  number: 0.61382 against 0.64206
  setup: ViT-B/16, ImageNet 5-shot linear; pre-training set not stated in D.4
  quote: "No Pos. Emb. 0.61382 N/A N/A" / "1-D Pos. Emb. 0.64206 0.63964 0.64292"
  where: Table 8 p17
- claim: Hybrids beat pure ViT only at small budgets.
  number: none
  setup: R50+ViT against ViT, JFT pre-training
  quote: "hybrids slightly outperform ViT at small computational budgets, but the difference vanishes for larger models."
  where: p8
- claim: The model variants scale from 86M to 632M parameters.
  number: 86M, 307M, 632M
  setup: Table 1 configurations, based on BERT's
  quote: "ViT-Base 12 768 3072 12 86M"
  where: Table 1 p5
- claim: Self-supervised pre-training helps but trails supervised pre-training.
  number: 79.9%
  setup: ViT-B/16, masked patch prediction on JFT, 1M steps
  quote: "our smaller ViT-B/16 model achieves 79.9% accuracy on ImageNet"
  where: p9
- claim: A class token and global average pooling work about equally once the learning rate is set for each.
  number: none
  setup: ImageNet linear 5-shot over training epochs (Fig 9)
  quote: "the difference in performance is fully explained by the requirement for a different learning-rate"
  where: pp16-17
- claim: Depth is the best dimension to scale, and width helps least.
  number: 16 layers
  setup: base ViT of 8 layers, D=1024, patch size 32, 5-shot
  quote: "diminishing returns are already visible after 16 layers"
  where: p16
- claim: Attention distance is variable across heads in low layers and grows with depth, and large ViTs are more memory-efficient than ResNets.
  number: none
  setup: ViT-L/16 attention analysis; TPUv3 core batch-size timing
  quote: "large ViT models have a clear advantage in terms of memory-efﬁciency over ResNet models."
  where: p8, p19, p20

LIMITS
- Classification only. Detection and segmentation are named as open challenges (p9).
- Few-shot analysis is left as future work (p7).
- The dataset-size curve is not a pure size test: regularisation and epochs differ by dataset in Table 3 and p6.
- Compute efficiency may depend on "training schedule, optimizer, weight decay" (p6).
- JFT is in-house, so its results are not publicly reproducible on that data.
- The paper predates DeiT, so it offers no ImageNet-only recipe matching ResNets.
- No threshold in images is given.
- Table 8's pre-training set is unstated.

BUILDS ON: Vaswani et al. (2017), architecture; Devlin et al. (2019), class token, model sizes and masked prediction; Cordonnier et al. (2020), the closest prior model, with 2×2 patches; Kolesnikov et al. (2020), BiT baseline and transfer protocol; Wang et al. (2019) and Baevski & Auli (2019), cited with pre-norm and residual placement; Sun et al. (2017), JFT; Chen et al. (2020a), iGPT; Abnar & Zuidema (2020), attention rollout; Wu & He (2018) and Qiao et al. (2019), the BiT ResNet changes; LeCun et al. (1989), hybrid CNN input.

CODE: None in the paper. Footnote 1 (p1) points to github.com/google-research/vision_transformer.

FIGURES
- Fig 1, p3, model overview: shows patches, class token and encoder at a glance.
- Fig 3, p7, transfer to ImageNet by pre-training set: shows the crossover against the BiT band, which Table 5 cannot because it has no CNN rows.
- Fig 4, p7, linear 5-shot against JFT subset size: the cleanest data-size comparison, with no regularisation changes.
- Fig 5, p7, performance against pre-training compute: shows the hybrid gap vanishing.
- Fig 7, p9, filters, position similarity and attention distance: shows position embeddings learning 2-D structure.
- Fig 9, p17, class token against GAP: shows the learning-rate dependence.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction faults: small-caps headings are split ("16 X16 W ORDS"), ligatures survive ("ﬁ"), equations are partly garbled, and figure text is scattered. Tables are readable as flat rows. Quotes joining a line break use a single space.
- The paper contradicts itself on ViT-H/14: Table 5 gives 88.04 ImageNet and 97.56 Pets, while Table 6 gives 88.08 and 97.11, with no explanation.
- Other slips in the paper: Fig 13's caption says "(left)" twice, Fig 6 points to Appendix D.7 though attention maps are in D.8, and the subsets are 9M/30M/90M in text but the axis reads 10M/30M/100M.
- No embedded instructions found.
